newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian court delays ruling on Mineralbank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian court delays ruling on Mineralbank.

text.p: The Sofia City Court on Wednesday postponed for a second time a ruling on an insolvency suit filed against Bulgaria's state-owned Mineralbank, according to the sequestrator appointed by the central bank..
The ruling was delayed until November 25.
"The court postponed its decision due to lacking information about Mineralbank's accounts in foreign banks, needed to establish is financial state," sequestrator Venko Krastev told reporters.
The BNB placed Mineralbank under special supervision on May 17 and two weeks later filed the insolvency suit against it.
On June 19 the Sofia City Court delayed ruling on the suit and appointed legal experts to establish the relationship between Mineralbank's assets and liabilities.
The bank's debts to foreign banks amounted to $240 million, including some $140 million owed to entities grouped in the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ).
Mineralbank failed to redeem five billion yen worth of samurai bonds to Japanese investors which matured in mid-June.

The IBJ, the lead arranger of the bond issued through private placement and bought up entirely by Japanese investors, is in talks with Bulgarian authorities over means of repayment, which have not produced results so far.
Mineralbank had cumulative losses of 8.6 billion levs as of the end of 1995. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
